name: Mauao
bio: A 232-metre volcanic cone at the end of Mount Maunganui, with summit and base tracks.

name: Mount Maunganui Main Beach
bio: A long surf beach below Mauao, with lifeguards in summer and a busy cafe strip behind.

name: McLaren Falls Park
bio: A park beside a lake with a waterfall, forest walks, kayaking and camping.

name: Tauranga Historic Village
bio: A re-created 19th-century village of period shops and homes.

name: Whakaari / White Island
bio: New Zealand's most active volcano, steaming offshore; landings have been suspended since the 2019 eruption.

name: Ōhope Beach
bio: An 11-km white-sand beach with a patrolled swim area and pōhutukawa along the shore.

name: Kohi Point Scenic Reserve
bio: A coastal walk past old pā sites and viewpoints to Whakaari offshore.

name: Wai-O-Tapu
bio: A geothermal wonderland of coloured pools, a champagne-coloured lake and the Lady Knox Geyser that erupts on schedule.

name: Te Puia
bio: A cultural and geothermal park with the Pōhutu geyser, boiling mud pools and a Māori arts school.

name: Whakarewarewa Forest
bio: A forest of giant redwoods with walks, a treetop walkway and some of the country's best mountain-bike trails.

name: Polynesian Spa
bio: Natural hot mineral pools beside Lake Rotorua with a view across the water.

name: Waimangu Volcanic Valley
bio: The world's youngest geothermal valley, with a walk past steaming craters and a boiling lake.

name: Hell's Gate Geothermal Park and Mud Spa
bio: Steaming mud volcanoes and the largest hot waterfall in the Southern Hemisphere, with a mud spa.

name: Blue Lake
bio: A sapphire-coloured crater lake with a track around its shore and a sandy swimming beach.

name: Government Gardens
bio: A garden of Tudor-style buildings including the Rotorua Museum, beside the lakefront.

name: Skyline Rotorua
bio: A gondola up Mount Ngongotahā with views over the lake, and a luge ride down.

name: Lake Tarawera
bio: A large lake beneath Mount Tarawera, with cruises to the Hot Water Beach and views of the volcano.

name: Lake Waikaremoana
bio: A large lake ringed by forest and mountains, with a multi-day Great Walk around its shore.

name: Aniwaniwa Falls
bio: A series of cascades in the forest, reached by a short walk from the lake's visitor centre.

name: Lake Waikareiti
bio: A forested lake with an island in a lake, reached by a bush walk, with a hut and kayaking.
